items.title: Section: Twenty Angles on Five Aggregates — And Consciousness's Own Fivefold Analysis Begins With Where It Dwells

items.zh: 復次，云何識蘊差別？此亦五種應知。一、由安住故；二、由雜染故；三、由所依故；四、由住故；五、由異相故。云何安住？謂習欲者欲界諸識，執外色塵，名色安住。若清淨天色界諸識，執內名色，名俱安住。無色界識唯執內名，名名安住。是名識安住差別。
items.en:
The Chapter of Deciding Discernment on the Five Sense-Consciousness-Corresponding Ground and the Mind Ground, part four.
Fifth, consciousness's distinctions; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what are consciousness's distinctions?
Second, the explanation; first, stating and listing. This too is, in brief, five: by dwelling place, by defilement, by support, by station, and by differing aspect.
Second, explaining each; first, the distinction of dwelling place; first, the question posed. What is dwelling place?
Second, the explanation; first, dwelling in form. Those habituated to desire have desire-realm consciousness grasping external sense-objects — this is called dwelling in form.
Second, dwelling in both. The pure gods of the form realm have consciousness grasping internal name and form together — this is called dwelling in both.
Third, dwelling in name. Formless-realm consciousness grasps only internal name — this is called dwelling in name. Third, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of consciousness's dwelling place.

items.title: Section: Two Doorways of Defilement — And the Fire That Burns the Same Whether Fed by Straw or Dung

items.zh: 云何雜染差別？謂諸愚夫由二種門識被染污。一、於現法中，由受用境界門；二、於後法中，由生老等門。是名識雜染差別。云何所依差別？謂六所依，諸識隨轉。謂依眼等六處，六識身轉，如世間火，依糠、牛糞、薪札等轉。是名識所依差別。
items.en:
Second, the distinction of defilement; first, the question posed. What is the distinction of defilement?
Second, the explanation. Ordinary, unlearned beings are defiled through two doorways: first, within the present life, through the doorway of engaging sensory objects; second, towards a future life, through the doorway of birth, ageing, and the rest.
Third, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of consciousness's defilement.
Third, the distinction of what consciousness depends on; first, the question posed. What is the distinction of what consciousness depends on?
Second, the explanation. The six active consciousnesses each depend on their own corresponding sense-faculty — depending on the eye and the rest of the six faculties, the six bodies of consciousness manifest, just as worldly fire depends on husks, cattle dung, firewood, or wood chips to burn.
Third, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of what consciousness depends on.

items.title: Section: The Four Stations Where Consciousness Takes Root — A Teaching Aimed Directly at the Heretic's Own Sense of Self

items.zh: 云何住差別？謂四識住。如經言：有四依取，以為所緣，令識安住。
items.en:
Fourth, the distinction of station; first, the question posed. What is the distinction of station?
Second, the explanation; first, correctly distinguishing the characteristic; first, briefly stating it; first, presenting the essential nature. These are the four stations of consciousness.
Second, citing the scripture's own words. As the sūtra states: there are four bases of grasping, serving as the object that causes consciousness to take root.

items.title: Section: The Four Stations Named — Form, Feeling, Perception, and Formations — Through Three Modes of Attachment Each

items.zh: 謂識隨色住，緣色為境。廣說如經。乃至我終不說此識往於東方乃至四維；然我唯說於現法中，必離欲、影，寂滅、寂靜、清涼、清淨。
items.en:
Consciousness follows form and dwells there, taking form as its object — as explained at length in the sūtra, and so likewise through feeling, perception, and formations in turn.
...I never say this consciousness goes to the east, or to any of the four intercardinal directions; rather, I say only that within this very life, it becomes forever free of desire and of feeling's shadow, reaching quiescence, tranquility, coolness, and purity.

items.zh: 如是已顯經中如來所說諸識住相。從此以後，我當宣說此相差別。謂此經中，略顯識住及因緣相，識住、因緣二種邊際，識住、因緣二種寂止。

items.title: Section: Five Technical Terms Unpacked — From the Bases of Grasping to the Four Bonds That Fetter Every Being

items.zh: 當知此中，若諸煩惱事，若屬彼煩惱，說名依取。應知此二亦名所緣，所緣性故，有所緣故。由彼貪愛為煩惱緣，名趣所執事。由貪欲等四種身繫為發業緣，名緣所緣事。彼二隨眠所隨逐故，名建立事。
items.en:
One should know that, here, whatever is the ground of affliction, together with whatever affliction belongs to it, is called the bases of grasping.
One should know these two are also called the object, since one is the nature of what is grasped as object, and the other genuinely possesses an object of its own.
Because that craving serves as affliction's own condition, this is called the object of craving's pursuit.
Because the four bonds of craving and the rest serve as the condition generating karma, this is called the object bound by affliction's fetters.
Because the latent seeds of these two continue to follow the being, this is called the establishing factor.

items.zh: 若諸異生補特伽羅，未得厭離對治喜愛，由所潤識能取能滿當來內身；由此展轉能取能滿不能棄捨諸異生性；以於內身能取能滿故，於流轉中相續決定，是名為住。餘住因緣，如前應知。

items.title: Section: Two Outer Limits of the Station — Coming and Going Versus Simply Dying and Being Reborn

items.zh: 是名略說住及因緣相。有色界識有來有去，無色界識有死有生。又此二住乃至壽盡。又復此二生長、增益及廣大義，如前應知。齊是名為識住邊際及住因緣邊際。
items.en:
This, in brief, is called the station and its sustaining condition.
Consciousness belonging to a being with form comes and goes; consciousness belonging to a formless-realm being simply dies and is reborn.
These two kinds of station continue right up until the exhaustion of the lifespan.
Their growth, strengthening, and expansion should likewise be understood as already explained.
This, precisely, is called the outer limit of the station and the outer limit of its sustaining condition.

items.title: Section: Refuting the Real Self — Three Fatal Flaws in the Heretic's Doctrine, and the Store Clerk Who Was Never Truly Good or Bad

items.zh: 若復異此而施設者，當知唯有文字差別，非義差別，由所餘義境界無故。若他正詰，不知何答，亦由餘義境界無故。或復有能於後自然如理觀察，便自迷悶，謂我愚癡，作如是說。
items.en:
Should anyone propose an alternative account differing from this, one should know it differs only in wording, never in substance, since no such further reality can ever actually be found.
When genuinely challenged, such a person has no answer to give, again because no such further reality can be found.
Or, upon later reflecting naturally and correctly on the matter, such a person becomes quietly troubled, recognising their own foolishness, and says as much.

items.title: Section: Bringing the Sustaining Condition to Rest — Different Afflictions for Householder and Renunciant Alike

items.zh: 若聰慧者，於諸色愛乃至行愛所攝貪纏能永斷離，於煩惱分所攝發業四身繫纏亦能永斷。所以者何？由在家眾，依貪欲、瞋恚二繫發起諸業，攝受境界為因故，損害有情為因故。若出家眾，依戒禁取、此實執取二繫發起諸業，以戒禁取猶如貪欲，求生天故；此實執取猶如瞋恚，謗涅槃故。
items.en:
The genuinely wise are capable of permanently severing the entanglement of craving belonging to craving for form up through craving for formations, and equally capable of permanently severing the four karma-generating bonds belonging to affliction itself.
Householders generate karma through the two bonds of craving and aversion, respectively motivated by pursuing pleasant objects and by harming other beings.
Renunciants generate karma through the two bonds of misguided observance and false absolutization — misguided observance paralleling craving in seeking heavenly rebirth, false absolutization paralleling aversion in slandering nirvāṇa itself.

items.title: Section: The Four Bonds Are Purely Mental — And the Sustaining Condition Finally Reaches Its Own Complete Rest

items.zh: 當知四身繫唯在意地，分別所生故。從此以後，由多修習勝對治故，復能永斷貪愛、身繫二種隨眠。由此斷故，煩惱所緣色、受等境亦不相續，以究竟離繫故。由此所緣不相續故，有隨眠識究竟寂滅，於色、受等諸識住中不復安住，由對治識永清淨故。是名識住因緣寂止。
items.en:
One should know that all four bonds ("body" here meaning an accumulation) belong solely to the mental ground, arising through its own discrimination.
From this point on, through sustained cultivation of an increasingly superior antidote, one becomes capable of permanently severing both latent seeds — of craving attachment and of the bonds.
Because of this severance, the objects of affliction — form, feeling, and the rest — no longer continue, having become ultimately freed from bondage.
Because these objects no longer continue, the latent, afflicted consciousness reaches its own final cessation, no longer abiding within any of the stations of form, feeling, and the rest, consciousness having become permanently purified through this antidote.
This is called the cessation of the station's sustaining condition.

items.title: Section: The Station Itself Comes to Rest — Twelve Angles Beginning With the Three Gates of Liberation

items.zh: 又由當來因緣滅故，於內身分不取不滿，決定無有流轉相續，是名識住寂止。又復對治所攝淨識，名無所住。由彼因緣故，名不生長。由善修習空解脫門故，名無所為。由善修習無願解脫門故，名為知足。由善修習無相解脫門故，名為安住。如是不生長故，乃至安住故，名極解脫。
items.en:
Because the cause capable of generating a future embodiment has ceased, consciousness no longer takes hold of nor completes any inner rebirth, saṃsāric continuity being decisively ended — this is called the cessation of the station.
The purified consciousness subsumed under this antidote is called non-abiding. Because of this same cause, it is called cessation of growth. Through skilful cultivation of the gate of emptiness, it is called non-activity. Through skilful cultivation of the gate of wishlessness, it is called contentment. Through skilful cultivation of the gate of signlessness, it is called abiding. Thus, from cessation of growth through abiding, this is called ultimate liberation.

blocks.text: Fascicle 54 continues analysing the aggregates, starting with consciousness: where it "dwells", what holds it there, and how it finally comes to rest.
In the desire realm consciousness grasps outer sense-objects; in the form realm, inner name and form; in the formless realm, inner name alone.

The six consciousnesses arise dependent on the six faculties, "as worldly fire burns on husks, dung, or firewood". Master Cháng Bǎi: all consciousnesses share discernment; they differ only by what they rely on. Towards pleasant feeling craving arises, towards painful feeling hatred, in neutral feeling delusion.
Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders take consciousness as a self and the four other aggregates as its dwelling; the Buddha taught the four stations to refute that.

The substance of grasping is affliction arising on the aggregates. Craving is what pursues; the four bonds bind; their latent seeds follow the being. (Untranslated, 0595a14 and 0595a22: an outline of the passage, and how an ordinary being, moistened by craving, keeps taking a future body and so stays in saṃsāra.)
Beings of the desire and form realms pass between lives through an intermediate body; formless consciousness simply dies and is reborn.
"Any other account differs only in words, since no such further reality can be found." Master Cháng Bǎi: the soul outsiders posit is only words.

Householders create karma through craving and aversion; renunciants through misguided observances and false absolutes. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four bonds are joined with mental consciousness; first the manifest bonds are cut, then, by long cultivation, their seeds.

The cause of a future body has ceased, and the round of rebirth is ended. Master Cháng Bǎi: the purified consciousness no longer grasps or makes karma; this is 無所為, "nothing more to do". A bodhisattva still widely saves beings.
"Fire burns the same on straw or dung." Consciousness is not a self with a home; it is a process that arises wherever its conditions are.

quiz.q: How does the treatise match the three dwellings of consciousness to the three realms?
options: desire-realm consciousness grasping inner name is dwelling in name; form-realm consciousness grasping outer objects is dwelling in form; formless consciousness grasping name and form is dwelling in both, for it keeps a subtle body
desire-realm consciousness grasping name and form is dwelling in both; form-realm consciousness grasping outer objects is dwelling in form; formless consciousness grasps nothing

desire-realm consciousness grasping outer objects is dwelling in form; form-realm consciousness grasping inner name and form is dwelling in both; formless consciousness grasping only name is dwelling in name
the consciousness of all three realms grasps inner and outer objects alike, differing only in coarseness
quiz.why: The treatise assigns grasping of outer sense-objects to the desire realm, grasping of inner name and form to the form realm, and grasping of inner name alone to the formless realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: the consciousness of formless gods grasps only inner mental phenomena, abiding in absorption, dwelling in its own feeling, perception, and formations.

quiz.q: How does engaging objects defile consciousness in the present life? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of the three feelings?
options: hatred arises towards pleasant feeling, delusion towards painful feeling, and craving in neutral feeling
all three give rise only to craving, hatred and delusion arising only in a future life, so this doorway has one defilement alone
craving arises towards pleasant feeling, hatred towards painful feeling, and delusion in neutral feeling
none of the three gives rise to afflictions, which come only from volition
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: on moving towards pleasant feeling, craving arises; on taking painful feeling as object, hatred arises; and abiding in neutral feeling, delusion arises. So engaging objects in this life defiles consciousness through the three poisons that accompany the three feelings.

quiz.q: What simile does the treatise use for consciousness depending on its supports?
options: water taking the shape of its vessel, square or round
wind moving in space, unobstructed in coming and going, pervading everywhere and depending on nothing
a shadow following a body, moving as it moves
worldly fire burning in dependence on husks, cattle dung, firewood, or wood chips
quiz.why: The treatise says the six bodies of consciousness manifest in dependence on the six faculties, as worldly fire burns on husks, dung, or firewood. Master Cháng Bǎi: all consciousnesses share discernment as their nature, and differ from eye-consciousness through mental consciousness by their supporting faculty. As with fire, the name follows the support.

quiz.q: Why did the Buddha teach the four stations, and why are the contaminated four aggregates their substance?
options: to show consciousness is the true self, with the four aggregates as its home; contaminated aggregates free it, and so they are called its stations
to show consciousness has a location in the body; contaminated aggregates are its organs
to refute outsiders who take consciousness as self and four aggregates as its abode; contaminated aggregates stir craving, so consciousness delights to dwell
to urge rebirth in the four absorption heavens, of which contaminated aggregates are the result
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders take consciousness as self and the four aggregates as its abode, and the Buddha taught this to refute that attachment. The contaminated four aggregates are the substance of the stations because they stir craving and make consciousness delight to dwell in them; when contaminated consciousness takes the uncontaminated truths of cessation and path as object, no station is established.

quiz.q: The English has "the craving found within the aggregates, together with whatever belongs to that craving." What is the problem?
options: the Chinese speaks only of the form aggregate, so the plural "aggregates" is too broad and should become "form"
the Chinese speaks of wholesome phenomena, so "craving" reverses it
the Chinese speaks of the outsiders' self, which the English leaves out
the Chinese does not say craving; the English writes one reading into the text, for the substance of grasping is affliction and what belongs to it is the four aggregates
quiz.why: The Chinese says "affliction," not craving. Master Cháng Bǎi: the substance of grasping is affliction, the various afflictions arising on the aggregates; and the four aggregates belonging to those afflictions are the object of consciousness. The English narrows 煩惱 to craving, and its "whatever belongs to that craving" does not show that this means the aggregates.

quiz.q: Why does the treatise speak of "the establishing factor"?
options: because craving serves as affliction's own condition
because the four bonds serve as the condition generating karma, beginning with craving and including the others
because the latent seeds of these two continue to follow the being
because form and the rest all possess an object
quiz.why: The treatise gives three names: craving as condition of affliction is the object of craving's pursuit; the four bonds as condition of karma are the object bound by fetters; and the latent seeds of these two, following the being, are the establishing factor. Master Cháng Bǎi: these seeds accompany the life-form, produce karma and results, and so establish the five aggregates.

quiz.q: The English has "a being with form" rather than "the form realm" for 有色界. Why is this good?
options: 有色界 means only the form realm, so "a being with form" is in fact too wide and should revert to "form realm"
有色界 means gods with bodies, humans being excluded
有色界 covers desire and form realms, both linked by the intermediate state, which the formless lacks; the English avoids narrowing it
有色界 means the Buddha's body, unrelated to beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the desire and form realms link two successive lives by an intermediate-state body, whereas formless consciousness has no intermediate state, and so simply dies and is born. Thus 有色界 means all realms with form. The English "a being with form" keeps this, where "form realm" would wrongly exclude the desire realm.

quiz.q: What is 所餘義 in "no such further reality can be found," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the soul asserted by outsiders, which is words only, with no real referent
the suchness taught by the Buddha, seen only by noble ones
a fifth station beyond the four, which the treatise takes up later, so it is set aside here for now
the store-consciousness, of which outsiders are unaware
quiz.why: The treatise says any other account differs only in words, since no such further reality can be found. Master Cháng Bǎi: the soul set up by outsiders is called the further reality, and no such object exists; the soul is only words, with no real referent. It is consciousness that transmigrates, not a self.

quiz.q: Through which two bonds do householders and renunciants generate karma?
options: householders through misguided observance and false absolutization; renunciants through craving and aversion
householders through craving and misguided observance; renunciants through aversion and false absolutization, each pairing one bond of feeling with one of view
householders through craving and aversion; renunciants through misguided observance and false absolutization
householders and renunciants alike through all four bonds
quiz.why: The treatise pairs them: householders generate karma through craving and aversion, pursuing objects and harming beings; renunciants through misguided observance, which parallels craving in seeking heaven, and false absolutization, which parallels aversion in slandering nirvāṇa. Master Cháng Bǎi: what householders crave are the five sense-objects; what renunciants crave is rebirth in heaven.

quiz.q: The English has "all four bodily bonds belong solely to the mental faculty." What contradiction does it create?
options: the four bonds actually lie in the five sense-consciousnesses, so "mental faculty" misplaces them and should read "five senses"
身 means accumulation, not the body; "bodily" contradicts "solely mental," and 意地 is not the mental faculty
the four are afflictions of the body faculty, and 意地 is a copyist's error for 身地
there is no contradiction: afflictions start in the body and pass to the mental faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 身 means accumulation; the accumulated craving, hatred, misguided observance, and false absolutization bind beings to the three realms. These four are joined with mental consciousness, formed by the discrimination of the sixth consciousness. So "bodily bonds ... solely of the mental faculty" reads as a contradiction, and 意地 here is not the faculty 意根.

quiz.q: After the binding manifest afflictions are severed, what remains to be severed, and with what result?
options: with superior antidotes one severs the latent seeds of craving and the bonds, and the latent-afflicted consciousness finally ceases
with absorption one suppresses form and feeling so outer objects never appear again
nothing remains: severing the bindings is already final liberation, the seeds vanish by themselves, and no antidote is needed
one then severs the store-consciousness itself, ending all mind
quiz.why: The treatise first speaks of severing the manifest bindings, then says that from this point on, by much cultivation of a superior antidote, one severs both latent seeds. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of craving towards the four aggregates and of the four bonds are severed forever, and consciousness no longer loves form and the rest. Hence the latent-afflicted consciousness ceases.

quiz.q: What is the cessation of the station?
options: no idle thoughts arise now, and one rests in absorption for a while, all returning as before on emerging from it
the cause of a future body has ceased, no inner rebirth is taken or completed, and saṃsāric continuity has decisively ended
the first six consciousnesses are cut off, the store-consciousness alone remaining
consciousness moves from this body to a pure land elsewhere
quiz.why: The treatise says the cause of the future has ceased, and so no inner bodily portion is taken or completed, and saṃsāric continuity is decisively ended. Master Cháng Bǎi: the cause of gaining a future inner body is craving, which has been severed, so there is no grasping conditioned by craving towards a ripened body.

quiz.q: Through which gate of liberation are 無所為, contentment, and abiding each attained?
options: wishlessness gives 無所為; emptiness gives contentment; signlessness gives abiding
the gate of emptiness gives 無所為; wishlessness gives contentment; signlessness gives abiding
signlessness gives 無所為; wishlessness gives contentment; emptiness gives abiding, since emptiness is what rests most stably
all three gates give ultimate liberation alike
quiz.why: The treatise assigns 無所為 to the gate of emptiness, contentment to wishlessness, and abiding to signlessness. Master Cháng Bǎi on wishlessness: reflecting that the five aggregates are impermanent and suffering, one no longer wishes for any result, which is why it brings contentment.

quiz.q: The English has "purposelessness" for 無所為. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it, and what is the trouble with the English word?
options: doing nothing at all and no longer benefiting beings, which "purposelessness" exactly conveys and need not change
wandering without a goal; the English should be "wandering"
the purified consciousness no longer grasps and creates karma; "purposelessness" suggests pointlessness, which does not fit
practice not for fame or gain; the English should be "selflessness"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the purified consciousness no longer grasps and creates karma, and this is called 無所為. It describes freedom from karma-making, not lack of purpose; he adds that a bodhisattva still widely saves beings. The English "purposelessness" carries the sense of pointlessness, which is far from this.
